page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32-lssd is an ARM-based server instance powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz with 1.0 thread per core. The processor is equipped with 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 80 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. For local storage, it includes 2412 GB of NVMe SSD capacity spread across 6 local SSDs, but does not feature any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4a-standard-32-lssd demonstrates strong memory performance and database capabilities. The Passmark memory score and database operations both rank in the top tier, supported by a strong Redis SET performance of 69.35 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 3959.92 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 345.42 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Geekbench multi-core testing places the instance in the top tier with a score of 23030.0, while single-core performance remains in the average to strong range. For text processing, image processing, and software compilation, the server consistently registers strong results, though ray tracing and LLM prompt processing fall into average tiers.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 Neoverse-V2 architecture delivers high resource density and strong compute-per-watt characteristics. The inclusion of 2412 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage bundled directly with the instance makes it highly cost-effective for I/O-intensive workloads without requiring external storage attachments. However, the lack of hardware acceleration limits its utility for heavy machine learning training, though it handles medium-sized LLM inference with a strong text generation speed of 31.37 tokens per second. This server is highly suited for high-throughput database operations, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and static web serving.
